A second fresh, dedicated two-node topology ran the same candidate harness in `topology` mode against the committed synthetic catalog and native Ansible playbooks in `playbooks/test/fixtures/deploy-components`. Public ID `dns` selected the fixture consumer with the original limit containing only A. Its required managed provider (`docker`) resolved B; that provider's same-host prerequisite (`host-monitoring`) also resolved only B. The provider's support-only endpoint (`dcgm-exporter`) resolved A and authorized no provider apply. Synthetic bindings explicitly named B as provider and A as support.

The focused candidate regressions had 72 passing test/subtest events, zero fail/skip. Two scratch negative controls failed for the intended reasons: removing component flag registration produced `unknown flag: --component`; widening the leaf scope made real Ansible resolve A+B instead of only B. Existing stage/legacy checks independently passed. No rollback injection was performed: the missing-package arm demonstrates convergence after a bounded prerequisite removal, not transaction rollback after mutation failure.

Raw outputs were captured in the controlled Issue 251 artifact directory (machine chain, `production-arms`, `topology-arms`, their harness summaries and negative-control logs), outside source files. A known-value scan of 27 machine/CLI raw logs found zero occurrences of the synthetic password, in addition to the machine record's own scan above. All three domains, their overlays and DHCP reservations were removed using pilot teardown after successful validation; libvirt confirmed no owned domains remained. Other sessions' targets and services were preserved.

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

- Production service proof covers native `host-monitoring` on fresh Ubuntu 24.04, including missing bcrypt-tool repair. It does not prove FreeIPA enrollment repair, every deploy component, other operating systems, upgrade/decommission behavior or failure-path rollback.
- Multi-hop/per-host proof uses the explicitly synthetic catalog and native marker playbooks; it does not install DNS, Docker or GPU services. The production contract catalog and apply playbook were unchanged.
- This change deliberately avoids `site.yml` union-tag execution; it does not resolve the separate site-wide scoping issue #224.
- No private repository/workflow was accessed or changed. `docs/deploy-ci.md` documents the public integration and generic components-input route. Full-suite/race validation is assigned to GitHub CI, separately from these local/target results.
- The host `/tmp` had no free inodes. Controller commands ran as the original user in a private mount namespace whose `/tmp` mapped to an owned artifact directory; host `/tmp` and existing files were untouched. Remote hosts used their native filesystems and services.
- The machine closure conservatively lists unresolved Ansible inputs; this is exact-candidate evidence and does not claim automatic reuse across later execution-affecting revisions.
